subject: Behavioral Economics
title: Trial and Error in Games
description: A micro-lesson that makes Trial and Error in Games usable.

hook.text: A poker beginner bluffs randomly and loses. After 100 hands, she bluffs selectively and starts winning.

buildup.text: Reinforcement learning: repeat actions that worked, avoid actions that failed. No theory needed.

discovery.text: Erev and Roth showed reinforcement learning explains lab behavior better than Nash equilibrium in many simple repeated.

twist.text: Reinforcement learning can lock into bad strategies. If an early lucky win follows a bad play, the learner repeats.

climax.text: Early luck distorts learning. To improve, track why you won, not just that you won. Process matters more than outcome.

punchline.text: Winning by luck teaches nothing. Winning by process teaches everything.

quiz.question: What is the danger of reinforcement learning in games?
options: It always finds the optimal strategy quickly
It can lock into bad strategies if early luck reinforces poor choices
It requires reading complex strategy books
